steps.title: Import React and useState
steps.instruction: Import React and useState from the 'react' library to build the security demonstration component.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in both React and the useState hook from the 'react' package.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: importing React and useState
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: The React library and useState hook are available for use in the component.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported React and useState, which are essential for building React components with state management.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're importing both React and useState from 'react'. Check your import statement syntax.
steps.feedbackWrong: The imports aren't quite right. Remember to import both React and useState from the 'react' library using the correct syntax.

steps.title: Create the main SecurityDemo component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named SecurityDemo that will contain all security demonstrations. The component should return null for now.
steps.hint: You can use either a function declaration or an arrow function. Remember to export the component.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';

// Create the SecurityDemo component here
steps.expectedOutcome: A functional component named SecurityDemo is created and exported.
successCriteria: The SecurityDemo component is defined and returns null. The component is exported as default.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the main SecurityDemo component that will hold our security demonstrations.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you've created a component named SecurityDemo that returns null and is exported.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component isn't quite right. You need to create a functional component named SecurityDemo that returns null and is exported.

steps.title: Initialize state for user input
steps.instruction: Inside your SecurityDemo component, initialize a state variable called 'userInput' using useState to store user-entered data. Set its initial value to an empty string.
steps.hint: Use the useState hook you imported earlier. The syntax is: const [userInput, setUserInput] = useState('');
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a state variable 'userInput' initialized to an empty string, ready to store user input.
successCriteria: The component contains a useState call that declares 'userInput' and 'setUserInput' variables with an initial value of empty string.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully initialized state to track user input. This is essential for handling form data securely.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're using useState with the correct syntax: const [userInput, setUserInput] = useState('');
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. Remember to use the useState hook to create a state variable called 'userInput' with an initial value of empty string.

steps.title: Initialize state for security messages
steps.instruction: Inside your SecurityDemo component, initialize a state variable called 'securityMessages' using useState to store security-related feedback messages. Set its initial value to an empty array.
steps.hint: Use the useState hook you imported earlier. The syntax is: const [securityMessages, setSecurityMessages] = useState([]);
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: state for storing messages
const [messages, setMessages] = useState([]);
steps.expectedOutcome: Your component will have a state variable 'securityMessages' initialized as an empty array, ready to store security feedback.
successCriteria: The component contains a state variable 'securityMessages' initialized with useState([]).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully initialized state to track security messages.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using useState with an empty array as the initial value for 'securityMessages'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. Initialize a state variable called 'securityMessages' with an empty array using useState.

steps.title: Create input sanitization handler
steps.instruction: Inside your SecurityDemo component, create a function called 'sanitizeInput' that takes a string parameter and returns a sanitized version by removing HTML tags.
steps.hint: You can create a function that uses a regular expression or replace method to strip HTML tags from the input string.
steps.expectedOutcome: A sanitizeInput function is defined inside the component that can remove HTML tags from input strings.
successCriteria: The component contains a function named 'sanitizeInput' that accepts a string parameter and returns a sanitized string with HTML tags removed.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created a sanitization function that helps prevent XSS attacks by removing dangerous HTML tags from user input.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a function, but make sure it's named 'sanitizeInput', accepts a string parameter, and removes HTML tags from the input.
steps.feedbackWrong: The sanitizeInput function isn't properly defined. Create a function inside the component that takes a string and removes HTML tags.

steps.title: Create input validation handler
steps.instruction: Inside your SecurityDemo component, create a function called 'validateInput' that takes a string parameter and checks if it contains suspicious patterns like '<script>' or 'SELECT'.
steps.hint: Define a function that uses includes() or test() with a regular expression to detect dangerous patterns in the input.
steps.expectedOutcome: A validateInput function that can detect potentially dangerous input patterns.
successCriteria: The validateInput function is defined inside the component and checks for suspicious patterns in the input string.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created a validation function that helps prevent injection attacks by checking for dangerous patterns in user input.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a function, but make sure it properly checks for suspicious patterns like script tags or SQL keywords.
steps.feedbackWrong: The validateInput function isn't defined correctly. Create a function that takes a string parameter and checks for dangerous patterns.

steps.title: Create security check handler
steps.instruction: Create a handler function called 'handleSecurityCheck' that calls both the sanitizeInput and validateInput functions.
steps.hint: Define a function that calls the two existing functions. You can place it after the validateInput function.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function named handleSecurityCheck that calls both sanitizeInput and validateInput.
successCriteria: The handleSecurityCheck function is defined and calls both sanitizeInput and validateInput.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created a security check handler that combines both sanitization and validation.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a function, but make sure it calls both sanitizeInput and validateInput.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try creating a function named handleSecurityCheck that calls both sanitizeInput and validateInput.

steps.title: Add main container and heading
steps.instruction: Inside your SecurityDemo component's return statement, add a main container div with a heading that introduces frontend security concepts.
steps.hint: Add a <div> wrapper and an <h1> or <h2> element with text about web security.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component returns a div container with a heading element containing introductory text about frontend security.
successCriteria: The return statement contains a <div> wrapper with a heading element (e.g., <h1> or <h2>) that includes text about web security concepts.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've set up the main UI structure with a security-focused heading.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a container, but make sure to include a heading with text about frontend security.
steps.feedbackWrong: The return statement should contain a div wrapper with a heading element about web security.

steps.title: Add input field and wire onChange to update userInput state
steps.instruction: Inside your SecurityDemo component's return statement, add a textarea element with a placeholder 'Enter text to test security...' and wire its onChange event to update the userInput state variable.
steps.hint: Use the onChange event handler to call setUserInput with the textarea's current value (event.target.value).
steps.expectedOutcome: A textarea input field appears in the UI that updates the userInput state when text is typed.
successCriteria: A textarea element is added inside the main div
The textarea has a placeholder attribute
The textarea's onChange event updates the userInput state
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added a controlled textarea input that updates state on change.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a textarea, but make sure it's properly wired to update the userInput state via onChange.
steps.feedbackWrong: The textarea input isn't properly connected to update state. Check the onChange handler and state variable name.

steps.title: Add security check button and wire onClick to handleSecurityCheck
steps.instruction: Add a button element with the text 'Check Security' inside your component's return statement, and wire its onClick event to call the handleSecurityCheck function.
steps.hint: Use the <button> tag with an onClick attribute that references your handler function.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding a button with click handler
<button onClick={handleClick}>Submit</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: A button labeled 'Check Security' appears in the UI that will trigger security validation when clicked.
successCriteria: The button element with text 'Check Security' is added and its onClick event is wired to call handleSecurityCheck.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the security check button with proper event wiring.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a button, but make sure it has the correct label and onClick handler.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button isn't properly configured. Check that you have a <button> element with onClick={handleSecurityCheck} and the text 'Check Security'.
